function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker service itself. To start Docker Desktop or Docker Engine, you typically use services or Docker Desktop UI. On Windows, you can start Docker via the Docker Desktop application or via PowerShell: Start-Service com.docker.service. Or if using Docker Engine installed as a service, you can use net start com.docker.service. Alternatively, you can use Docker Desktop's CLI: docker-machine start default. But the user likely wants to start Docker engine. So we need to execute a command to start the Docker service. We have a tool to run commands. We'll call functions.cmd_controller_execute with command "net start com.docker.service". That will start the Docker service. If they want to start Docker Desktop, maybe "Start-Service com.docker.service" in PowerShell. Let's do "net start com.docker.service". Also we might check if it's already running. But just starting it should be fine.

We need to output the result of executing the command. We'll call the function.
